obligation_candidates.canon_label: Define `route_target` as the canonical navigation-and-focus contract.
exact_tokens: Define `route_target` as the canonical navigation-and-focus contract.
Define `OpenSubject` as the canonical identity-native source-open contract.
Keep `OpenFile` as the path-based editor contract only.

State the resolution chain directly: `route_target` may land on a surface that then invokes `OpenSubject`; `OpenSubject` may resolve to `OpenFile`; `OpenSubject` may resolve to a transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source buffer
The three contracts are now distinct: `route_target` = navigation; `OpenSubject` = identity-native source open; `OpenFile` = path-based editor open
notes: The three-contract split is the key architectural decision: route_target owns navigation, OpenSubject owns identity-native source open, OpenFile owns path-based editor open. If route_target carries source-buffer realization details it will bloat. If OpenSubject carries panel/tab/shell destination semantics it collapses back into a second route contract.
resume_url sits on the route_target side (restores app navigation context), NOT the OpenSubject side.
